items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: So we made "Two Little Fishes and Five Loaves of Bread" and it was a big hit.

ctx.x: I'll tell you how that came about, Dan. You know, early I told you that I came from a long line of religious singers and you could be banished from the clan if you sang gospel songs or if you sang songs in a rhythm and that thing, you know what I mean. Although, back in those days, the Church of God in Christ people were doing it, but they were doing it in a church atmosphere. Church background and church setting. So finally, one day Milt Gabler asked Mayo to have me come down to see him. And a guy had written a…

whatever he did with them and all. So they asked me would I consider to work with Rosetta Tharpe. Well you know Rosetta Tharpe tuned her guitar funny and sang in the wrong key and the meter sometimes were not exact. She could sing and all that, but then she was a folk singer more or less. So I told Mayo I'd have to think about it. And then he sent...they sent Rosetta Tharpe's mother to see me and to explain to me that if a song were played, if the mind teaching was right, then that was not against that feeling…

I'll get the musicians. I'll take care of everything, you don't have to worry. Oh, I'd show her how to move that fret up on her guitar so it'd be in the right key, show her how to...just let her play her heart out, and I would play with her, you know, and make the musicians play, and I use good jazz musicians. And I think that that was one of the things --- (recording interruption) Now where were we?
